summary: Extraction pass over 20 stored Malta documents (legal notices for the GRP, IIP, MRVP, exceptional-services scheme, MPRP and the 2027 Individual Tax Programme; Act XXI of 2025; the CJEU judgment and press release in C-181/23; Commission press releases and COM(2019) 12; IMF 2019 Article IV; two Komunita Malta notices). The legal notices hold no statistics; they add 33 fee and threshold rows the dataset lacked (dependant due diligence, passport and bank fees for the IIP; deposits, due diligence, administrative and permit fees for the 2020 scheme; regional, financial-asset, donation and later-addition amounts for the MPRP; agent licence fee; GRP renewal fee). The IMF report adds the overall balance excluding IIP proceeds projected for 2019-2024 and structural and structural-primary balances excluding IIP for 2016-2024 (two new indicators proposed). Five events added, including the L.N. 159 of 2025 clause ending investment-route applications not approved before 29 April 2025. COM(2019) 12 is the same report as intl-ec-com-2019-12; only the Malta fees were taken here.

events.title: Commission writes to Malta that the IIP may breach sincere cooperation
events.description: By letter of 1 April 2020 the Commission told Malta that investor citizenship schemes such as the 2014 IIP, which involve the 'sale' of Union citizenship, could breach the principle of sincere cooperation. Malta replied with details between April and October 2020.
events.quote: By letter dated 1 April 2020, the Commission indicated to the Republic of Malta that investor citizenship schemes such as the 2014 investor citizenship scheme

events.title: 2020 Citizenship (Amendment) Act adopted, creating the exceptional-services route
events.description: Malta adopted the 2020 act amending art. 10(9) of the Maltese Citizenship Act (naturalisation for exceptional services, including by investors); it does not apply to applications filed before it came into force. The detailed 2020 regulations followed on 20 November 2020.
events.quote: On 28 July 2020, the Republic of Malta adopted the 2020 act.

events.title: Commission files infringement action against Malta (C-181/23)
events.description: Action for failure to fulfil obligations under Art. 258 TFEU brought on 21 March 2023, limited to the 2020 investor citizenship scheme; hearing 17 June 2024, Advocate General's opinion 4 October 2024.
events.quote: ACTION for failure to fulfil obligations under Article 258 TFEU, brought on 21 March 2023

events.title: MRVP no longer ends after four years of continuous stay or long-term residence
events.description: L.N. 189 of 2017 deleted the cessation grounds in reg. 9(1)(b) (becoming a long-term resident) and 9(1)(f) (staying legally and continuously in Malta for four years or more) and extended certificates to dependants born or adopted later and to spouses of approved children.
events.quote: paragraphs (b) and (f) of sub-regulation (1) thereof shall be deleted

events.title: MPRP agents may be paid promotional support; pending MRVP applicants barred for 24 months
events.description: The MPRP regulations let the Residency Malta Agency pay registered agents promotional support for each successful application (reg. 25), require all applications to go through licensed agents, and bar applicants with a pending MRVP application from applying under the MPRP for 24 months; from 29 March 2021 no new MRVP applications may be made.
events.quote: As from 29th March 2021, all new applications shall be governed by these regulations and no new application for a certificate may be made under the Malta Residence and Visa Programme Regulations.

events.title: Investment-route applications not approved before 29 April 2025 lapse
events.description: L.N. 159 of 2025 renamed the regulations "Granting of Citizenship by Naturalisation on the basis of Merit Regulations", deleted Part IV (naturalisation by direct investment), the cap of 400 a year and 1,500 in total, the fee provisions and the fee and residence-permit schedules, and replaced them with a proposal-letter and Evaluation Board procedure for merit applicants. Its transitional clause says applications under Part IV that the Minister had not approved for naturalisation before 29 April 2025 (the date of the CJEU judgment) cease to have effect.
events.location: regs. 16, 22, 24 and 25 (PDF p. 14 and 17, printed B 1609 and B 1612)
events.quote: any applications submitted under Part IV of the Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services Regulations which had not been approved for naturalisation by the Minister under the said Part IV prior to 29 April 2025, shall cease to have effect.

ledger.contains: European Commission press release of 20 Oct 2020 opening infringement procedures (letters of formal notice) against Cyprus and Malta over investor citizenship schemes; background on the 2019 report, the April 2020 letters and the July 2020 Parliament resolution; also a letter to Bulgaria. No programme numbers. The Malta event (letter of formal notice) is already in events.

European Commission press release of 29 Sep 2022 referring Malta to the Court of Justice: timeline (formal notice 20 Oct 2020, additional notice 9 Jun 2021, reasoned opinion 6 Apr 2022, suspension for Russian and Belarusian nationals 2 Mar 2022), the IIP cap of 1,800 successful main applicants (already in the IIP launch event), and notes on Cyprus and Bulgaria. Only unquantified programme figure: "several thousand investors and their family members" naturalised (not a number). All Malta events are already in events.

Komunita Malta press release of 23 Jul 2025: amendments to the Citizenship Act to comply with CJEU C-181/23, discontinuing the Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services programme and removing references to the transaction and agents; minister and lawyer quotes. No numbers. The event is already in events.

Komunita Malta notice of 2 Sep 2025 listing Act XXI of 2025 (in force 24 Jul 2025) and L.N. 159 of 2025 (merit-based naturalisation rules); also mentions the citizenship-by-descent deadline extension and adoption clarification (out of scope). No numbers. The event is already in events.

Act XXI of 2025 (assented 24 Jul 2025, passed 23 Jul 2025) amending the Maltese Citizenship Act: deletes the individual investor programme definition, rewrites art. 10(9) as naturalisation by merit, renames regulator complaint provisions, and new art. 27(4) keeping applications filed before entry into force under the old rules. Also citizenship-by-descent dates moved to 1 Aug 2028 and adoption rules (out of scope). No programme numbers; the event is already in events.

CJEU Press Release No 52/25 (29 Apr 2025) summarising the judgment in C-181/23 that the 2020 investor citizenship scheme infringes Art. 20 TFEU and Art. 4(3) TEU. No numbers. The judgment event is already in events (from the judgment itself).

CJEU Grand Chamber judgment of 29 Apr 2025 in C-181/23 (EUR-Lex HTML page). Legal framework (Treaty articles, Maltese Citizenship Act art. 10, IIP 2014 cap of 1,800, 2020 regulations: EUR 600,000/750,000 contribution, EUR 10,000 deposit, EUR 700,000 property or EUR 16,000 rent, EUR 10,000 donation, 36/12 months residence, EUR 50,000 per dependant, cap of 400 a year and 1,500 in total), pre-litigation timeline (1 Apr 2020 letter, 20 Oct 2020 formal notice, Malta's replies of 18 Dec 2020, 6 Aug 2021 and 6 Jun 2022, 9 Jun 2021 additional notice, 2 Mar 2022 suspension for Russians and Belarusians, 6 Apr 2022 reasoned opinion), parties' arguments, findings and costs. The fee and cap figures repeat L.N. 437 of 2020 and are already in program_terms and events from that source, so not repeated. Added: events for the 1 Apr 2020 Commission letter, the 28 Jul 2020 act and the 21 Mar 2023 filing (other dates already in events). Malta's procedural replies and the hearing date are court procedure, not programme changes. No statistics. For decision: para 36 also lists ten nationalities still excluded from the 2020 scheme (Afghanistan, DR Congo, Iran, North Korea, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Venezuela, Yemen); the existing 2022-03-02 event (same source) could mention this in its description.

European Commission report COM(2019) 12 final (23 Jan 2019) on investor citizenship and residence schemes in the EU. Same report as intl-ec-com-2019-12 (and grc-eu-com-2019-12): a different PDF download with identical text. Malta content: IIP terms (EUR 650,000 contribution, EUR 150,000 investment, EUR 350,000 property or EUR 16,000 rent: already in program_terms from L.N. 47 of 2014), total fees EUR 8,200 main applicant and EUR 5,500 spouse (added here), 12-month e-Residence requirement, four-tier due diligence, exclusion of nationals of Afghanistan, Iran and North Korea (rule without an amount or date), the 1,800 cap and the plan to raise it by another 1,800 (already in events from this source), regulator, agents, 2017 national money-laundering risk assessment. Rest: EU law analysis, security/AML/tax risks, Bulgaria and Cyprus citizenship schemes, investor residence schemes in 20 Member States, candidate and visa-free countries (Montenegro, Turkey, Moldova); no statistics anywhere.
ledger.to_do: Non-Malta rules are not extracted here because the same report is stored as intl-ec-com-2019-12 and should be extracted once there: Croatia's HRK 100,000 (about EUR 13,500) minimum residence investment (footnote 41), Cyprus 6-month residence permit before naturalisation and Council of Ministers Decision 834 of 13.9.2016 requiring residence permits (p. 4-6). Bulgarian EUR 650 and Cypriot EUR 7,000 fees, the BGR working group and HUN notes are already taken from intl-ec-com-2019-12.

ledger.contains: IMF Country Report 19/68: Malta 2019 Article IV press release, staff report (macro developments, housing, fiscal, financial sector, AML/CFT, external assessment, DSA) and Executive Director statement. Programme content: IIP proceeds in the fiscal accounts (Table 2 memorandum lines: overall balance, structural balance and structural primary balance excluding IIP proceeds, 2016-2024), the authorities' estimate that IIP export receipts were about 1% of GDP a year in 2015-2017 (Annex IV), qualitative mentions of IIP demand, housing and AML risks, and a DSA stress test without IIP revenue. Already in data: 2015-2017 receipts and overall balance excl. IIP for 2016-2018. Added: overall balance excl. IIP projections 2019-2024 and the two structural series 2016-2024 (two new indicators proposed). The p. 20 text table repeats the same structural figures for 2018-2023 (same source, not repeated). The DSA "IIP proceed shock" (debt 33% of GDP at end of projection, 3 points above baseline) is a debt scenario rather than a programme figure and is not recorded; Figure 3 and the Figure 5 stress-test chart have no printed IIP values. The rest of the report (growth, banks, NIIP, labour) is not about the programme.

L.N. 167 of 2013, Global Residence Programme Rules (in force 1 Jul 2013; English text, the Maltese pages carry no extractable text): definitions, qualifying property thresholds (EUR 275,000 / 220,000 purchase; EUR 9,600 / 8,750 a year rent), application through an authorised registered mandatary with a EUR 6,000 fee (EUR 5,500 for owned property in the south), beneficiary conditions, 15% tax on remitted foreign income with a EUR 15,000 minimum, 35% on other income, cessation (incl. more than 183 days in another jurisdiction, EUR 5,000 penalty for late notification), information exchange, schedule of southern localities. Added the EUR 8,750 rent and EUR 5,500 fee; the other amounts and the start date were already recorded. The tax rates, the late-notification penalty and the 183-day rule are conditions rather than prices and are described here only. No statistics.

L.N. 47 of 2014, Individual Investor Programme Regulations (published 4 Feb 2014; English text): definitions (70% of contributions to the National Development and Social Fund), concessionaire and licensed Approved Agents (annual licence fee, amount not stated), applicant requirements, eligibility and exclusion criteria, application process (90/30-day steps, approval in principle, EUR 350,000 property or EUR 16,000 rent and EUR 150,000 investment held 5 years, certificate 6-24 months after application, 12 months residence), refunds, deprivation, cap of 1,800 main applicants, NDSF governance, publication of names, revocation of L.N. 450 of 2013, and the Schedule of contributions and fees. Already recorded: contributions, main-applicant due diligence fee, property, rent, investment, launch event with cap and NDSF share. Added: the EUR 10,000 non-refundable deposit, due diligence fees for dependants (EUR 5,000 / 3,000 / 5,000 / 5,000), passport fee EUR 500 per person and bank charges EUR 200. No statistics.

L.N. 288 of 2015, Malta Residence and Visa Programme Regulations (English text): definitions (EUR 30,000 contribution incl. EUR 5,500 non-refundable fee, EUR 250,000 qualifying investment, property EUR 320,000 / 270,000 or rent EUR 12,000 / 10,000 a year), certificate rights and monitoring, application via registered agents, eligibility, conditions (property and investment held 5 years, EUR 100,000 foreign income or EUR 500,000 capital), cessation (EUR 15,000 late-notification penalty), information exchange, agent registration (agent share of the contribution capped at 10%), schedule of southern localities. All amounts except the income alternative were already recorded; added the EUR 100,000 income requirement. The penalty and the 10% agent-share ceiling are conditions, not prices, and are described here only. No statistics; the launch event is already recorded.

L.N. 189 of 2017, MRVP (Amendment) Regulations (English text): Identity Malta replaced by the Malta Residence and Visa Agency; contribution redefined as EUR 30,000 plus EUR 5,000 per parent or grandparent; wider dependant definition; property thresholds restated (EUR 320,000 / 270,000); EUR 5,500 application fee restated; new EUR 5,000 supplementary fee for adding family members later; police certificates from age 14; Schengen-wide sickness insurance; EUR 100,000 income / EUR 500,000 capital restated; cessation grounds (b) long-term residence and (f) four years continuous stay deleted; Marsa added to southern localities. Already recorded: the EUR 5,000 parent contribution and an event for the agency change. Added: the EUR 5,000 supplementary fee and an event for the deleted cessation grounds. Restated amounts unchanged from L.N. 288 of 2015 are not repeated. No statistics.

L.N. 437 of 2020, Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services Regulations (English text): definitions (dependants incl. children to 29 and parents over 55), general provisions, disqualifications, eligibility assessment with four-tier due diligence, Part III merit route (8 months residence, Evaluation Board), Part IV direct-investment route (36 months residence or 12 with the higher contribution, EUR 700,000 property or EUR 16,000 rent for 5 years, EUR 10,000 donation), cap of 400 a year and 1,500 in total, non-refundable fees, continuing obligations, deprivation, data protection, repeal of the IIP regulations with savings, First Schedule (EUR 600,000 / 750,000 contribution with EUR 10,000 deposit, EUR 50,000 per dependant; due diligence and administrative fees), Second Schedule (residence permit fees), Third and Fourth Schedules (competent bodies, oath). Already recorded: contributions, dependant contribution, property, rent, donation and the launch event with the caps. Added: the deposit, due diligence fees (EUR 15,000 / 10,000 / 15,000), administrative fees (EUR 1,000 eligibility, EUR 500 citizenship) and residence permit fees (EUR 5,000 / 1,000). No statistics.

L.N. 121 of 2021, Malta Permanent Residence Programme Regulations (English text): definitions (EUR 2,000 NGO donation; property EUR 350,000 / 300,000; rent EUR 12,000 / 10,000), agents (mandatory, register, duties, sanctions), application (EUR 10,000 fee on application; EUR 500,000 assets of which EUR 150,000 financial), Letter of Approval in Principle and payment deadlines, rights, dependants and later additions, eligibility and due diligence, conditions (property and capital for 5 years), cessation, data protection, confidentiality, promotional support payments to agents, transitional rules for MRVP, First Schedule (EUR 40,000 administration fee; contribution EUR 28,000 owned / EUR 58,000 rented, EUR 7,500 per parent or grandparent; later additions EUR 7,500 / 5,000) and Second Schedule (southern localities). Already recorded: EUR 40,000 fee, EUR 500,000 capital, EUR 28,000 / 58,000 contributions, EUR 350,000 property, EUR 12,000 rent, launch event. Added: the southern/Gozo property and rent thresholds, EUR 150,000 financial assets, EUR 2,000 donation, EUR 10,000 first fee instalment, contributions for parents and later-added family, and an event on agent payments and the MRVP transition. No statistics.

L.N. 122 of 2021, MRVP (Amendment) Regulations (published with the MPRP, English text): agents redefined as those licensed and on the MPRP register; EUR 2,000 NGO donation; monitoring of beneficiaries; option to pay an additional EUR 68,000 (rented) or EUR 38,000 (owned) contribution instead of the EUR 250,000 qualifying investment, paid to the National Development and Social Fund; deadlines to conclude pending applications (end-2021, 31 Mar 2022, or nine months from approval in principle); later inclusion of family members against a EUR 5,000 supplementary fee; income/capital affidavit to cover five years after issue. Already recorded: the EUR 38,000 / 68,000 contributions, EUR 2,000 donation and the wind-down event with deadlines. Added: the EUR 5,000 fee for adding a spouse, adult child or parent. No statistics.

L.N. 310 of 2024, MPRP (Amendment No. 2) Regulations, in force 1 Jan 2025 (English text): dependent children limited to under 29; single property threshold EUR 375,000 and rent EUR 14,000 for Malta and Gozo (southern discount and Second Schedule deleted); first fee instalment raised to EUR 15,000; assets test EUR 500,000 (EUR 150,000 financial) or EUR 650,000 (EUR 75,000 financial); administration fee and contribution for each dependant; health insurance wording; agent criteria notice one month; transitional rule; new First Schedule (EUR 50,000 fee, EUR 5,000 per dependant; contribution EUR 30,000 owned / EUR 60,000 rented, EUR 5,000 per dependant; disabled dependants exempt). Already recorded: all schedule amounts, property, rent, EUR 650,000 test and the price-change event. Added: the EUR 15,000 first instalment and the EUR 75,000 financial-asset minimum. No statistics.

L.N. 146 of 2025, MPRP (Amendment) Regulations (published 22 Jul 2025, English text): agents licensed directly by the Residency Malta Agency (qualifications, eligibility, EUR 500,000 professional indemnity cover, processing within six months, revocation, surrender; old licences valid to 31 Dec 2025); parents must not be in full-time employment; one-year renewable temporary residence permit while an application is processed; guidelines on use of the property during absences; per-dependant contribution abolished; new First Schedule (EUR 60,000 fee with EUR 15,000 on application and EUR 45,000 after approval in principle; EUR 7,500 per dependant other than spouse, minor or disabled child; EUR 37,000 contribution for owned or rented property); Third Schedule (EUR 5,000 annual agent licence fee); transitional rule applying the new fees to unconcluded applications filed after 1 Jan 2025. Already recorded: EUR 60,000 fee, EUR 7,500 dependant fee, EUR 37,000 contribution and the price-change event. Added: the EUR 5,000 agent licence fee (and the EUR 15,000 first instalment row from L.N. 310 of 2024 left open, as it continues). No statistics.

L.N. 159 of 2025, Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services (Amendment) Regulations (English text): renames S.L. 188.06 as merit-based naturalisation regulations; new definitions (dependants incl. children under 29); eligibility and disqualification wording; applications filed directly or through an approved professional; deletes the eligibility assessment (regs. 8-10), Part IV direct-investment route and the 400/1,500 cap (regs. 15-19, 21), fee and repeal provisions (regs. 30-31) and the First to Fourth Schedules; new proposal-letter procedure (reg. 11A) with four-tier due diligence and application stage (reg. 11B: 8 months residence, property, language, ties); Evaluation Board composition and remuneration; oath within six months; continuing obligations; deprivation; transitional clause ending investment-route applications not approved before 29 Apr 2025. No amounts (fees left to the Agency) and no statistics. Added an event for the deletion of the investment route and the lapse of unapproved applications. For decision: this transitional clause is a primary-source basis for the programme note that new applications stopped on 29 Apr 2025.

L.N. 195 of 2026, Individual Tax Programme Rules (in force 1 Jan 2027, English text): definitions (EUR 700,000 owned or EUR 14,000 a year rented qualifying property in Malta or Gozo), four special tax statuses (global resident; EU/EEA/Swiss resident; retired pensioner; UN pensioner), EUR 8,500 application fee, five-year status renewable for EUR 2,500, statuses granted or applied for by 31 Dec 2026 continuing to 31 Dec 2031, beneficiary conditions (pension shares 75% / 40% for the pensioner statuses), 15% tax on remitted foreign income with minimum tax EUR 35,000 (global and EU/EEA/Swiss), EUR 15,000 (retired pensioners), EUR 20,000 (UN pensioners), 35% on other income, cessation (incl. 183 days abroad), penalties (EUR 5,000; EUR 10,000; EUR 500-19,250 for mandataries), information exchange and mandatary rules. Already recorded under mlt-grp: fee, property, rent, EUR 35,000 minimum tax (notes give the pensioner minimums) and the publication event. Added: the EUR 2,500 renewal fee. The pensioner statuses are not investment-residence schemes and are described in notes only; penalties are conditions, not prices. No statistics.
